module: luamqtt I/O loop: runs several MQTT clients (and user functions) in the same thread, in non-blocking mode with a small network timeout, which enables keep_alive PINGREQs and reconnection. Only works with the standard luasocket connectors.
usage:
local ioloop = require('libs/luamqtt/mqtt/ioloop')
local loop = ioloop.get()
loop:add(client)
client:start_connecting()
-- in the game's own loop:
loop:iteration()
notes: run_until_clients is blocking; in the game, call iteration() periodically instead (e.g. from onUpdate) so as not to freeze the thread.

get.desc: Returns the default ioloop (singleton), created on demand.

__init.desc: Initializes the instance with timeout, sleep and sleep_function (default socket.sleep).

add.desc: Adds an MQTT client or a loop function. For a client, calls client:set_ioloop(self) to associate it with the loop.

returns.desc: true, or false and error message.

remove.desc: Removes a client or a function from the ioloop.

returns.desc: true, or false and error message.

iteration.desc: Performs one iteration: calls _ioloop_iteration of each client and each added function, then sleeps args.sleep seconds if sleep > 0.

can_sleep.desc: If no network timeout has occurred yet during the iteration, calls sleep_function(args.timeout) once (socket.sleep by default) so as not to spin idle.

run_until_clients.desc: Blocking loop: iterates as long as at least one client remains in the ioloop.
